question: Does Engine::Initialize already include device creation, and what is the exact object chain?
answer: Yes. Engine::Initialize allocates and constructs a GraphicsEngine and then calls GraphicsEngine::CreateDevice(window, settings) on it, testing the returned bool.

sequence.mov [rsi+0x1F8], rax: the new GraphicsEngine is stored at Engine+0x1F8
sequence.test al, al / jne 0x7485c: success path continues; failure path calls 0x143900 (log object) and 0x146040 (format the message)

evidence_chain_closed.earlier: 0x256f0 reads mov rax,[0x180421428]; mov rdx,[rax+0x1F8]; mov rcx,[rdx+0xC0]; call [rax+8]
evidence_chain_closed.now: Engine::Initialize stores the GraphicsEngine at Engine+0x1F8
evidence_chain_closed.conclusion: 0x421428 therefore holds the Engine object, and Engine+0x1F8 holds the GraphicsEngine. The two facts were derived independently and agree.

why_the_publisher_never_mattered: Device creation is inside Engine::Initialize, so a host that constructs an Engine with the original constructor and calls the original Initialize gets a real GraphicsEngine and a real device without needing to know which code wrote the global.

host_contract.step1: WinWindow::WinWindow() at 0x217710, then WinWindow::Initialize at 0x2179b0 to obtain a real EWindow
host_contract.step2: GraphicsEngineSettings::GraphicsEngineSettings() at 0x906e0 (defaults to the direct3d11 plugin name, length 10)
host_contract.step3: Engine::Engine() at 0x72930 on a caller buffer. The constructor writes only up to +0x198, but Engine::Initialize writes and reads as far as +0xC27, so the buffer must be at least 0xC28 bytes.
host_contract.step4: Engine::Initialize at 0x743d0 with arguments (EWindow*, settings const&, bool, FileSystem*, std::string const&, bool, string, string, string, string, bool)
host_contract.step5: after success the engine global used by other engine code is the Engine object itself; a host must publish its own pointer there because the game side publisher is not identified

not_yet_established: the meaning of the four trailing std::string arguments and the three booleans
the minimum Engine object size for certain (only the +0x358 write is observed so far)
whether Engine::Initialize requires any earlier subsystem to exist

object_sizes.engine_min: 0xC28 bytes (highest offset touched by Initialize is 0xC27)
object_sizes.graphics_engine: 0x1C0 bytes (the value passed to operator new immediately before the GraphicsEngine constructor)
object_sizes.win_window: at least 0x48 bytes based on the fields its constructor and Initialize write

subsystem_fields_written_by_initialize: Initialize populates many later fields of the Engine object, including +0x3D8, +0x410, +0x418, +0x428, +0x50, +0x668, +0x670, +0x678, +0x688, +0x690, +0x698 and +0x6A0, which is consistent with it standing up a large set of subsystems rather than a single device.
